results.name: Joby Aviation to acquire Resonant Sciences in $500 million defense deal – AeroTime
results.content:
Joby Aviation announced on August 11, 2026, that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Resonant Sciences, a Dayton, Ohio-based defense technology company, for approximately $500 million.
Joby plans to fund the acquisition with approximately $450 million in cash and $50 million in Joby common stock, with certain Resonant employee stockholders retaining an ongoing equity stake. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approval. The announcement comes a day after Joby’s closest rival made an almost identical move. Archer Aviation agreed to acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid subsidiaries on August 10, 2026, a deal built around Insitu, the profitable ScanEagle and Integrator drone maker that generates more than $200 million in annual revenue.
Founded in 2015, Resonant designs, manufactures and delivers radio frequency (RF) and mission systems for US national security customers and is a global leader in low-observability technologies, structures and subsystems. The roughly 250-person company also works in advanced sensing, electronic countermeasures, communications and autonomous systems.
Resonant operates approximately 105,000 square feet across seven buildings in the Dayton area, with a further 125,000 square feet under construction, alongside facilities in Virginia, West Virginia, Michigan, Colorado and North Carolina. Combined with Joby’s own manufacturing footprint in Ohio, the acquisition will give the companies close to one million square feet of manufacturing, integration and testing space in the Dayton region.

results.content:
# Joby Aviation to scale defence business through $500 million Resonant Sciences acquisition  
[Share on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Faerospaceglobalnews.com%2Fnews%2Fjoby-acquires-resonant-sciences-500m-defence%2F)  
[Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u%5Bscheme%5D=https&u%5Bhost%5D=aerospaceglobalnews.com&u%5Bpath%5D=%2Fnews%2Fjoby-acquires-resonant-sciences-500m-defence%2F)  
[Copied to clipboard Share on X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Faerospaceglobalnews.com%2Fnews%2Fjoby-acquires-resonant-sciences-500m-defence%2F&text=Joby%20Aviation%20to%20scale%20defence%20business%20through%20%24500%20million%20Resonant%20Sciences%20acquisition)  
J[oby Aviation](https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/tag/joby-aviation/) is buying defence technology company Resonant Sciences for $500 million, giving the [electric air-taxi](https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/tag/air-taxi/) developer a sizeable defence business as it continues to spend heavily on getting its commercial aircraft through certification and into passenger service.  
Under the agreement, Joby will pay $450 million in cash and $50 million in stock. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. Resonant Sciences, led by Co-Founder and CEO J. Micah North, will then operate under its own name as Joby’s dedicated defence business.
## What is Resonant Sciences?  
Resonant, founded in 2015 and based in Dayton, Ohio, develops and manufactures radio-frequency, sensing and mission systems for US national security customers. Its technology covers advanced radar, navigation and communications, electronic countermeasures, low-observability systems and autonomous applications.  
The company has about 250 employees and its products are qualified on more than 20 air platforms, according to the material supplied by the companies.  
That gives Joby something it does not have to build from scratch: an established defence engineering and manufacturing operation with national security customers, specialised technology and personnel working on programmes that can already move through the defence procurement system.  
The deal is more than an expansion into another market. It shows how quickly the business plans of the leading US electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) companies are changing. Joby and rival Archer Aviation are still pursuing air taxis, but both are now putting greater weight on military and government applications that can reach customers sooner.
## Resonant Sciences gives Joby’s Aviation an established US defence technology platform  
Joby’s approach is more concentrated. Rather than acquiring several businesses, it is taking control of one established defence technology company and making it the foundation of a dedicated defence division.  
Resonant has already expanded its manufacturing capacity and nearly doubled its highly skilled technical workforce since Cerberus invested in the company in 2023. Cerberus said Resonant has also moved technologies from research and development into production-ready offerings and expanded its customer and programme base.  
Cerberus Senior Managing Director and Co-Head of Supply Chain Michael Palmer said the investment had focused on building the operational base needed to scale.  
“Over the past three years, we expanded manufacturing capacity, advanced key technologies into production, and deepened relationships with customers,” Palmer said.  
Resonant CEO J. Micah North said the company had retained its focus on national security customers while expanding its ability to execute more programmes.  
“Cerberus understood what makes Resonant different – our culture, our focus on the warfighter, and our drive to move quickly and solve difficult problems,” North said.  
“Demand for advanced defense technology is growing rapidly, and Resonant has built the technology, customer relationships and manufacturing capabilities required to meet it,” North added.

results.content:
# Joby Aviation to Acquire Resonant Sciences To Expand Its Defense Business  
Joby Aviation has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Resonant Sciences, a Dayton, Ohio based defense technology company, for roughly $500 million. The deal marks a major step forward for Joby's defense business, adding scale through a profitable, fast growing company already supporting active U.S. national security programs.
#### Who Resonant Is  
Founded in 2015, Resonant employs about 250 people, more than 90% of whom hold security clearances. The company designs and delivers advanced radio frequency and mission systems for U.S. national security customers, ranging from next-generation antennas and radomes to electronic countermeasures.  
Resonant is also recognized as a global leader in low-observability design. Its electronics, apertures, and radomes are qualified across more than 20 commercial and defense airframes, and the company handles full payload integration and aircraft modification for its customers, which include the U.S. Government and major prime contractors.
#### Deal Terms and Timing  
The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory review and other standard closing conditions. Joby plans to fund the acquisition with about $450 million in cash and $50 million in Joby common stock, with the share price for that portion fixed at signing. Some Resonant employee shareholders will receive part of their payout in Joby stock, keeping a stake in the combined company going forward.
